note: Original finding text lives in ../raw/internal-app-layer.md; each entry here carries id, title, original severity and the verdict fields.

verdicts.title: Legacy-format transcript projection runs beside the identity format
verdicts.note: ProjectEntryParts routes Format != TurnFormatIdentity to ProjectTurnParts (apptranscript.go:445); placement.go:81 stamps Format on every written entry; 1268e1282e is dated 2026-09-26; build.go has 31 'communicate' mentions; flush_communicate.go is 102 lines. The ~1000 LOC legacy-only figure is an estimate I did not re-count. This is a product decision, not a refactor.
verdicts.revised_fix_plan: Ask Jesse first. Do not rewrite users' transcripts in place without a backup and explicit approval (user work preservation). Option to weigh: normalize legacy entries into identity-shaped entries in memory at the read boundary (no file rewrite) so only one projection path remains. Bump index projectionID and update the transcript-read-model row in docs/product/subsystems.md.

verdicts.title: Two subscription-admission resolver generations coexist in appserver
verdicts.note: V1/V2 coexistence and the repeated condition at server.go:1995/1999 are real; local server/server.go:506 sets V1, hub app_rpc.go:1060 sets V2. But the 'same decode' claim is off: the hub inline decode returns Invalid on bad JSON and does not require Subscribe, while decodeSubscriptionAdmissionParams (server/server.go:556) returns ok=false on bad JSON and when Subscribe is false. They differ on purpose, so one shared helper must keep those semantics.
verdicts.revised_fix_plan: Port the local resolver to return SubscriptionAdmissionResolution, delete V1 field, safeResolveAdmission and the V1 branch, rename V2. Share only the method/param struct decode (returns params, decodeErr); keep each embedder's mapping of decodeErr (Invalid vs not-subscribe) explicit. Add a TDD test for local invalid-target behavior. Keep the fuzz target on the shared decoder.

verdicts.title: Dead and test-only API on the appserver subscription and notifier surface
verdicts.note: Repo-wide non-test grep: package Subscribe/ReplaceSubscriptions, Connection.Subscribe/ReplaceSubscriptions, Subscriptions.IsSubscribed, Subscriptions.Connections, Notifier.RetainedWindow/RetainedWindowCurrent, Server.SetBeforeSubscriptionGate have no production callers (only definitions); callers are cmd/evener-hub/*_test.go and appserver tests. Safe to delete after repointing tests.

verdicts.title: appserver/server.go is a 2.3k-line mix with a 14-hook test seam
verdicts.note: server.go is 2327 lines; appserver tests 10,406 lines in 35 files vs about 3,600 prod; captureSubscription takes 8 params plus variadic resolveTarget (server.go:1406-1415); locks mu, projectionMu, deliveryMu, hydrationMu, admissionMu, responseMu, sendMu present. Pure file split is safe.

verdicts.title: Two mechanisms decide which requests leave the serial worker
verdicts.note: Both mechanisms exist (concurrentDispatchMethod server.go:1606 with a hard-coded product method list; ConcurrentRequest cfg; two go func blocks in executeOrdered). They are documented, tested, and have deliberately different backpressure. Moving the table to embedders is reasonable but is placement/taste, not drift; severity overstated.
verdicts.revised_fix_plan: Optional: have embedders pass the slow-read method set via config and merge the two goroutine blocks into one helper; keep both backpressure behaviours and the unknown-method-stays-serial test.

verdicts.title: ServerConfig has accreted redundant knobs and pass-through wrappers
verdicts.note: Logf/logf and olderProtocolVersion wrapper confirmed. Navigation is NOT unused: hub sets static Navigation={Version:1} exactly when its navigation provider is nil (app_rpc.go:1028-1034), so deleting it requires the hub to supply a constant func. AdapterNativeInitialize has only a test setter (server_coverage_test.go:138) but drives three production sites (server.go:553,562,1030, including skipping ValidateMutationParams), so removal changes what that test covers.
verdicts.revised_fix_plan: Inline olderProtocolVersion; collapse Logf/logf into one; make Navigation a single func field (hub passes a constant func). Treat AdapterNativeInitialize separately: check what server_coverage_test needs before deleting.

verdicts.title: Subscription lifecycle context keys and unsubscribe paths
verdicts.note: Seven context key types in server.go (1056-1059, 1205-1207) and two public unsubscribe entry points (hub UnsubscribeLifecycle x3, local Unsubscribe x3) confirmed. The 'unlocked routedSeq read is not evidently safe' concern is refuted: the closure is invoked as currentSequence() at server.go:1507 inside captureSubscription while projectionMu is still held (taken at :1434, released in abortAfterUnlock/after cut), and Broadcast writes routedSeq under projectionMu (:459-460). It is safe, only non-obvious.
verdicts.revised_fix_plan: Same consolidation plan (one unsubscribe target value under one key, merge the two unsubscribe functions), plus a comment at server.go:1283 stating the closure runs under projectionMu. Do after findings 2 and 3; race lane in CI only.

verdicts.title: projectTurn is a 414-line switch with pasted ThreadItem scaffolding
verdicts.note: projectTurn spans 484-898 (414 lines) confirmed. Six systemMessage literals in the function (531,546,565,603,627,658), not seven (the 7th, PreludeTurn:103, is a different function). The claim that goal-continuation/steering arms omit TranscriptEntryIndex is refuted: apptranscript.go:658-664 sets TranscriptEntryIndex, as do all six. Timestamp pattern: 5 sites in apptranscript.go (492,804,879,922,1062), logical_turn.go:223, overlay.go:461, and the helper itself at notice.go:50, so entryStartedAt already exists and could be reused. Savings are smaller than stated (~-60, not -120).
verdicts.revised_fix_plan: Reuse entryStartedAt (or a millisOf helper) at the 7 sites; add systemMessageItem helper for the six literals; split projectTurn by turn kind afterwards. Drop the 'pin the TranscriptEntryIndex inconsistency' step, there is none.

verdicts.title: Three full-transcript scans compute overlapping totals; second failure counter
verdicts.note: Single functions each have one production caller (FailedToolCallsFromFile: app_threadread.go:1481; UsageTotalFromFile: agent/jobs_activity_past.go:325) while DerivedTotalsFromFile has one (app_threadread.go:1439). apptranscript failureCounter (failed_tool_calls.go:97) duplicates the name-learning of transcript.FailureCounter (agent/transcript/failures.go:81), which the index builder uses (build.go:149). Duplication real. But UsageTotalFromFile is called through agent's own activityUsageCache (a separate TurnCache) and only needs usage; pointing it at the combined scan makes the activity-usage path also do failure counting and holds a larger memo.
verdicts.revised_fix_plan: First do the safe part: replace failureCounter with transcript.FailureCounter (add a narrow-decode observe entry) and drop the duplicated failure rule. Then decide per caller whether the combined scan's extra work is acceptable for activity usage; keep the usage-only scan if CI benchmarks show regression. Keep parity tests.

verdicts.title: TurnCache.invalidate deletes pre-activation sidecar files
verdicts.note: turn_cache.go:247-248 remove path+'.appwire-index.json' and '.journal'; 'appwire-index' appears in no other Go file; current sidecar is DirFor(path)=path+'.index' (transcriptindex/dir.go:6). Dead remnant.

verdicts.title: Exported API without production callers and pass-throughs
verdicts.note: Non-test grep: ScanPrelude, ItemTurnProjectionFromEntries, ItemTurnsFromEntries, HasTranscriptKeysPrefix have no callers. ImagesFromContent, StringifyToolContent, WebSearchProjection, DefaultImageProjector are used only inside apptranscript. ExitCodeFromToolState is a one-line forward with one caller (overlay.go:524). Correction: appitempaging.ValidateCandidates is called 6+ times in production (appsource), so it is the exported entry, only the unexported twin is the pass-through: unexport/merge into one, do not delete the API.

verdicts.title: Comments cite symbols and files that no longer exist
verdicts.note: No definitions of matchesLastAssistantMessage, recordAssistantMessage, appTurnSnapshot, mergeAppThreadItem, appThreadItemIdentityMatches; server/appwire_turns.go does not exist (also still cited in appwire-client/typescript/model.ts:179 and reducer.ts:139, and app_threadread.go:1506). index.go:25-34 has a 'v8:' paragraph above formatVersion=6/projectionID v8. Real doc drift but comment-only; severity low.

verdicts.title: ToolIntentFromArguments copied three times in Go
verdicts.note: apptranscript.go:227, agent/doctor/transcript.go:331 are byte-for-byte equivalent; agent/transcript_render.go:1749 toolIntent differs (uses parseArgs and scalarString, so non-string scalars are accepted). All three can import agent/transcript (doctor and transcript_render already do), so the stated 'different module' premise is stale. Fifteen-line functions, low drift cost.
verdicts.revised_fix_plan: Add transcript.ToolIntent in agent/transcript with a table test that pins the scalarString difference first; migrate apptranscript and doctor (identical), and move transcript_render only if the scalar behaviour is intended to match.

verdicts.title: Delegate-info mapping and cloning duplicated four times
verdicts.note: appwireDelegateInfo (projector:466), appDelegateFromDetailedStatus (server/appwire_runtime.go:2827) and appwireDelegateFromAgentStatus (app_threadread.go:1278) map the same ~45 fields positionally; only the projector truncates (activitybound) and sets LogicalOwnerSessionID/ReportPreview. The projector comment says the read path bounds the same way elsewhere, so live-vs-saved drift is unconfirmed. cloneAppwireDelegateInfo (projector:552) equals appwire.cloneDelegateInfo (clone.go:284) field for field; pointer clone helpers duplicated 4x (cloneBoolPointer, cloneInt64Pointer, cloneServerBool/Int64, cloneHubBool/Int64) while generic clonePointer is unexported in appwire. Source structs are three different types in three packages, so a single conversion may not be possible without a shared type.
verdicts.revised_fix_plan: Stage 1 (safe): export appwire.CloneDelegateInfo/CloneQueueState, delete projector clone copies and the 6 pointer helpers (use a generic helper). Stage 2: only if the agent and events status structs can be unified, add one conversion; otherwise keep the mapping per source and add a field-coverage test that fails when EvenerDelegateInfo gains a field a mapping omits.

verdicts.title: AppEventProjector.Project is a 356-line switch
verdicts.note: Project spans 81-437 (356 lines). Job started/finished literals are not 13 identical fields: JobStartedData vs JobFinishedData are different types with different fields (Finished adds Reason, Exhaustion*, Resumable, ExitCode, OutputBytes), so only the trailing JobsTreeUpdated block (339, 378) and shared field subset duplicate. The map[string]any for thread/closed is deliberate: struct Reason is omitempty and the map always emits 'reason' (comment :421-426), so a typed struct cannot be byte-identical without changing the appwire tag and the TS client contract.
verdicts.revised_fix_plan: Extract jobsTreeNotification and withTaskRouting helpers and split the switch into per-domain methods. Leave thread/closed as is (or change the appwire tag deliberately with the TS client in the same PR). Trim the M7/v1 history comments.

verdicts.title: appitempaging.cloneThreadItem drifted from appwire's clone; two cursor codecs
verdicts.note: Aliasing confirmed: appitempaging/page.go:209-224 copies Position, Images (shallow), OutputImages, Raw only; appwire/clone.go:58 also clones StartedAt, CompletedAt, DurationMS, ExitCode. The cursor-codec half is weak: apphistory.contentCursor (paging.go:278-306) and appitempaging cursor.go carry different payload structs and fences; sharing a codec saves little and risks invalidating held cursors.
verdicts.revised_fix_plan: TDD red test for pointer aliasing in RegroupTurnFragments, export appwire.CloneThreadItem and delete appitempaging.cloneThreadItem/cloneTurnWithoutItems. Skip the cursor-codec unification unless a third cursor appears.

verdicts.title: Production code carries seams that exist only for coverage or a single test
verdicts.note: marshalContextCompaction (live_notice.go:19, comment says test-only); InstallReadObserverForTesting (read_stats.go:23); four testKill* globals (index.go:113-137), SetUpdateLogRecordsForTest (:55), HoldSidecarLockForTest (:1407); exitProcess/executeTemplate globals in appwiredoc/main.go:31-32 and exitProcess in appwirets/main.go:22 all confirmed.

verdicts.title: Protocol generators carry private reflective type walkers
verdicts.note: Confirmed that appwiredoc registerReflectType (main.go:179) keeps the first claimant (typeNames[name] !seen) while appwirets registry.addNamed panics on divergent same-name types (emit.go:424). Doc/TS disagreement is possible. But the TS collision test compares emitted TS interfaces, a backend-specific check, so a shared walker needs a pluggable comparator; the size estimate (-90/+60) is optimistic.
verdicts.revised_fix_plan: Smallest fix: make appwiredoc panic on a same-named different reflect.Type (prev != t) with a unit test. Only extract a shared walker if a third generator appears.

verdicts.title: apphistory.Read and fill are long with a redundant re-encode loop
verdicts.note: The second loop is NOT redundant: item bytes are a documented lower bound (paging.go:244-246), and the loop at :263-276 measures the real regrouped page including turn envelopes against pageContentBytes. It runs once for normal pages and repeats only for oversized windows. Extracting reconcileChanges from Read is a fair readability change; dropping the loop would break the page size bound.
verdicts.revised_fix_plan: Extract reconcileChanges and trimToPageBudget as pure moves; keep the full-page encode check (at most bound it by dropping several items per iteration, guarded by a size-boundary test).
